evidence_packet.evidence_text: Altrincham hotel to stop housing asylum seekers, MP says - BBC News Image caption, Cresta Court Hotel in Altrincham has been used to house male asylum seekers since November 2024 By Kevin Fitzpatrick , Greater Manchester political reporter and Rachael Lazaro , North West Published 43 minutes ago A hotel that has been the scene of anti-immigration demonstrations and counter-protests over the last two years will stop housing asylum seekers, the local MP has said. Labour's Conor Rand confirmed the 148-bedroom Cresta Court in Altrincham, Greater Manchester, would "end housing asylum seekers within the next three months as the remaining residents are moved out of the hotel". The local Conservative group claimed the decision came off the back of its "two years of relentless campaigning". A spokesperson for the Home Office said the closure was part of its policy of "closing every asylum hotel and moving asylum seekers into alternative accommodation, including former military sites". Several protests have taken place outside Cresta Court since it began being used to house asylum seekers in 2024, attracting a large police presence. Image source, Reuters Image caption, Anti-immigration protesters gathered outside the hotel in August last year Rand told BBC Radio Manchester : "Hotels are not suitable places to house asylum seekers. "It's bad news for community, bad news for taxpayers, and bad news for people themselves seeking asylum. "It's a practice that should never have been started." Image caption, Labour MP Conor Rand says hotels are "not suitable" places to house asylum seekers In 2023, at the peak of the policy of housing asylum seekers in hotels, 400 were in use at a cost of £9m a day, according to the government. title: Demolition of Rochdale's Seven Sisters flats devastating, residents say

evidence_packet.title: Demolition of Rochdale's Seven Sisters flats devastating, residents say
evidence_packet.lead: Residents who have been informed that their flats will be bulldozed say they will continue to "fight"
evidence_packet.summary: Residents who have been informed that their flats will be bulldozed say they will continue to "fight"
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Demolition of Rochdale's Seven Sisters flats devastating, residents say - BBC News Image caption, Christina Hartley and Roy Kitcher say the flats are "home" and they do not want to move By Davinia Ramos , Reporting from in Rochdale and Rebecca Brahde , North West Published 1 hour ago Residents of a town's tower blocks which are set to be demolished have said it is "devastating" but they will continue to "fight" the decision. Rochdale's Seven Sisters tower blocks, which contain 766 flats, will be replaced by about 600 homes , social landlord Rochdale Boroughwide Housing (RBH) has said. Demolition of the tower blocks was first proposed in 2017 but was ruled out in 2023 after a local campaign against it, but residents began moving out in October 2025 over long-term safety concerns. Roy Kitcher and Christina Hartley, who have lived in one of the blocks for 14 years, said they were left "upset" and "angry". RBH said demolition was the only "realistic and affordable" option. Kitcher said: "It's devastating news - why they want to knock them down, I don't know." The couple are one of 78 households yet to accept an offer of another home. "This is home and I want to stay here, I don't want to be moving out again," Kitcher added. Hartley said: "I'm just so upset about it and angry." She said the council had asked her to look at accommodation, however it was not in the town. "I want to stay in Rochdale, I'm a Rochdale girl born and bred and I won't move until they find me somewhere round here," she said. Image source, Reuters Image caption, The seven sisters in Rochdale were built in the 1960s A local campaign, previously backed by Rochdale Council, had appealed for the buildings to be refurbished rather than demolished. evidence_packet.summary: The Manchester park will host a series of 25,000-capacity concerts over two weekends next summer
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Large outdoor concerts are due to return to Manchester's Platt Fields Park next summer, with LCD Soundsystem named as the first headliner The American rock band will perform at the park in Fallowfield on 30 July 2027, with Young Fathers, Cowboy Hunters and DJs Erol Alkan and Luka Una also on the bill Organisers said the concert would be part of a series of shows, each with a capacity of 25,000, taking place over two weekends in late July and early August The events, called PlattForm, are being organised by The Warehouse Project, SJM Concerts and Live Nation, with more artists due to be announced in the coming weeks Platt Fields Park previously hosted the Parklife music festival from 2010 to 2012, before it moved to Heaton Park in 2013 to accommodate growing crowds Other music festivals have since taken place at the park, including Flashback Festival in 2022 and 2023

title: Is an autism or ADHD diagnosis key to helping people?

evidence_packet.title: Is an autism or ADHD diagnosis key to helping people?
evidence_packet.lead: People with autism and ADHD say the help and understanding they receive can be crucial
evidence_packet.summary: People with autism and ADHD say the help and understanding they receive can be crucial
evidence_packet.evidence_text: In the past 25 years, there has been a huge rise in the number of people seeking a diagnosis for autism or attention deficit hyperactivity disorder More than 1,255,000 people in England are currently waiting for diagnosis or treatment for those conditions and wait times can be more than seven years The NHS is now trying to steer more people away from a formal diagnosis and towards targeted help, which could be given much more quickly, but will that be enough for people who have spent years questioning why life seems so difficult? For Dawn Cameron, school years were a tough time The 43-year-old, from Wigan in Greater Manchester, said she was "seen as shy and odd and I was just really, really struggling with the school environment" She said her "biggest issues" came in multi-sensory environments, where there were "smells and noise [and] your senses are just overwhelmed"

title: The rare opportunity to examine centuries-old Coptic manuscripts

evidence_packet.title: The rare opportunity to examine centuries-old Coptic manuscripts
evidence_packet.lead: Hundreds of people were able to encounter their heritage first-hand at a church in Stockport
evidence_packet.summary: Hundreds of people were able to encounter their heritage first-hand at a church in Stockport
evidence_packet.evidence_text: More than 400 Coptic Christians have had the rare opportunity to examine manuscripts which were centuries old - thanks to a library in Manchester People travelled from across the UK to read the manuscripts, which were written in Coptic - an ancient Egyptian language - with some dating back to the 10th century The historical Coptic and Ethiopian manuscripts are normally housed in The University of Manchester's John Rylands Library Dr Jeremy Penner, senior curator at the library, said there was "something quite remarkable" about a manuscript "finding itself once again among people who know its prayers, recognise its saints and continue its traditions" "These books may belong to the Rylands, but their stories belong to a much larger world," he said Among the manuscripts on display were biblical texts, Coptic liturgies and a Holy Week lectionary

evidence_packet.lead: A hotel that has been the scene of anti-immigration demonstrations and counter-protests over the last two years will stop housing asylum seekers, the local MP has said Labour's Conor Rand confirmed the 148-bedroom Cresta Court in Altrincham, Greater Manchester, would "end housing
evidence_packet.summary: A hotel that has been the scene of anti-immigration demonstrations and counter-protests over the last two years will stop housing asylum seekers, the local MP has said Labour's Conor Rand confirmed the 148-bedroom Cresta Court in Altrincham, Greater Manchester, would "end housing
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A hotel that has been the scene of anti-immigration demonstrations and counter-protests over the last two years will stop housing asylum seekers, the local MP has said Labour's Conor Rand confirmed the 148-bedroom Cresta Court in Altrincham, Greater Manchester, would "end housing asylum seekers within the next three months as the remaining residents are moved out of the hotel" The local Conservative group claimed the decision came off the back of its "two years of relentless campaigning" A spokesperson for the Home Office said the closure was part of its policy of "closing every asylum hotel and moving asylum seekers into alternative accommodation, including former military sites" Several protests have taken place outside Cresta Court since it began being used to house asylum seekers in 2024, attracting a large police presence Rand told BBC Radio Manchester : "Hotels are not suitable places to house asylum seekers

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Residents of a town's tower blocks which are set to be demolished have said it is "devastating" but they will continue to "fight" the decision Rochdale's Seven Sisters tower blocks, which contain 766 flats, will be replaced by about 600 homes , social landlord Rochdale Boroughwide Housing (RBH) has said Demolition of the tower blocks was first proposed in 2017 but was ruled out in 2023 after a local campaign against it, but residents began moving out in October 2025 over long-term safety concerns Roy Kitcher and Christina Hartley, who have lived in one of the blocks for 14 years, said they were left "upset" and "angry". RBH said demolition was the only "realistic and affordable" option Kitcher said: "It's devastating news - why they want to knock them down, I don't know." The couple are one of 78 households yet to accept an offer of another home

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Large outdoor concerts are due to return to Manchester's Platt Fields Park next summer, with LCD Soundsystem named as the first headliner The American rock band will perform at the park in Fallowfield on 30 July 2027, with Young Fathers, Cowboy Hunters and DJs Erol Alkan and Luka Una also on the bill Organisers said the concert would be part of a series of shows, each with a capacity of 25,000, taking place over two weekends in late July and early August The events, called PlattForm, are being organised by The Warehouse Project, SJM Concerts and Live Nation, with more artists due to be announced in the coming weeks Platt Fields Park previously hosted the Parklife music festival from 2010 to 2012, before it moved to Heaton Park in 2013 to accommodate growing crowds Other music festivals have since taken place at the park, including Flashback Festival in 2022 and 2023

evidence_packet.title: Rochdale's landmark Seven Sisters tower blocks to be demolished
evidence_packet.lead: A town's landmark tower blocks, which have dominated its skyline since the 1960s, are set to be demolished after years of uncertainty over their future Rochdale's Seven Sisters tower blocks, which contain 766 flats, will be replaced by about 600 homes, social landlord Rochdale Bo

evidence_packet.evidence_text: A town's landmark tower blocks, which have dominated its skyline since the 1960s, are set to be demolished after years of uncertainty over their future Rochdale's Seven Sisters tower blocks, which contain 766 flats, will be replaced by about 600 homes, social landlord Rochdale Boroughwide Housing (RBH) said Residents began moving out of the flats in October 2025 following concerns about their long-term safety but a local campaign, previously backed by Rochdale Council, had appealed for the buildings to be refurbished rather than demolished But RBH said replacing the buildings was the "only realistic and affordable way" to provide suitable homes for residents Refurbishment would have cost at least £269m and would have taken 12 years, RBH said Some 78 households have yet to accept an offer of another home

title: Is an autism or ADHD diagnosis key to helping people?

evidence_packet.title: Is an autism or ADHD diagnosis key to helping people?
evidence_packet.lead: In the past 25 years, there has been a huge rise in the number of people seeking a diagnosis for autism or attention deficit hyperactivity disorder More than 1,255,000 people in England are currently waiting for diagnosis or treatment for those conditions and wait times can be mo
evidence_packet.summary: In the past 25 years, there has been a huge rise in the number of people seeking a diagnosis for autism or attention deficit hyperactivity disorder More than 1,255,000 people in England are currently waiting for diagnosis or treatment for those conditions and wait times can be mo
evidence_packet.evidence_text: In the past 25 years, there has been a huge rise in the number of people seeking a diagnosis for autism or attention deficit hyperactivity disorder More than 1,255,000 people in England are currently waiting for diagnosis or treatment for those conditions and wait times can be more than seven years The NHS is now trying to steer more people away from a formal diagnosis and towards targeted help, which could be given much more quickly, but will that be enough for people who have spent years questioning why life seems so difficult? For Dawn Cameron, school years were a tough time The 43-year-old, from Wigan in Greater Manchester, said she was "seen as shy and odd and I was just really, really struggling with the school environment" She said her "biggest issues" came in multi-sensory environments, where there were "smells and noise [and] your senses are just overwhelmed"

evidence_packet.evidence_text: More than 400 Coptic Christians have had the rare opportunity to examine manuscripts which were centuries old - thanks to a library in Manchester People travelled from across the UK to read the manuscripts, which were written in Coptic - an ancient Egyptian language - with some dating back to the 10th century The historical Coptic and Ethiopian manuscripts are normally housed in The University of Manchester's John Rylands Library Dr Jeremy Penner, senior curator at the library, said there was "something quite remarkable" about a manuscript "finding itself once again among people who know its prayers, recognise its saints and continue its traditions" "These books may belong to the Rylands, but their stories belong to a much larger world," he said Among the manuscripts on display were biblical texts, Coptic liturgies and a Holy Week lectionary

The situation has now left the council with a toxic problem to deal with Town hall bosses are set to carry out ‘urgent’ works at Royton Library due to the need to tackle toxic asbestos. Asbestos is a fibrous mineral that was valued for its strength and fireproofing capabilities in old buildings and was widely used It is now banned from use, but if disturbed where it is still present, those fibres cause severe, incurable lung diseases. Around 5,000 people are estimated to die from asbestos-related issues every year The library was refurbished as part of a major £4m scheme which finished in 2024. However, earlier this year, the library had to shut suddenly and has remained closed since A council report said that in July 2026, library staff ‘reported that flooring in certain areas was becoming ‘bouncy’’ and ‘severe signs of dry rot’ were later discovered. Further investigations were carried out once the library closed

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Greater Manchester Police Greater Manchester's 400 Clean Air Zone cameras are now being used by police officers The cameras have been handed to police after the end of Clean Air Zone proposals Add to preferred sources Comments News Declan Carey Local Greater Manchester’s former Clean Air Zone (CAZ) cameras are now being used by the police to fight crime Around 400 CAZ enforcement cameras and more than 1,000 signs were installed around the region as part of previous plans to charge drivers of high-polluting vehicles up to £60 a day to use Greater Manchester’s roads But there was backlash to the Clean Air Zone charging scheme and the proposal was shelved in favour of a clean air plan instead It meant starting to take down around 1,300 signs at a cost of £600,000 , but the cameras stayed Greater Manchester Police (GMP) has now taken over the cameras and is already making use of the automatic number plate recognition technology to fight crime

He set himself up as a hired gun when he struggled to make a living after being released from prison His low fees reflected his desperation - and the fact he wasn't very good at his job. The father-of-one had failed to kill one man and missed a second target altogether Tragically, the third job saw an innocent shopworker gunned down in a case that exposed a deadly gang rivalry in Oldham and Bolton Henderson's previous crimes included robbing a Post Office and stealing £40,000 of drugs money. His first job came in November that year when he was told to shoot dead the guarantor for a man who owed a loan shark £30,000

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Trafford Trafford taxi driver, 76, taken to court after he's found to be picking up fares illegally The 76-year-old was suspended for failing to provide a medical report showing his fitness to drive Add to preferred sources Comments News Charlotte Fis A 76-year-old taxi driver has been disqualified from driving after continuing to illegally take fares despite having his licence revoked three years ago John Funna tried to deceive Trafford Council by taking illegitimate fares after he had been suspended as a taxi driver in September 2023 - but never returned his driver’s badges to Trafford Town Hall, Manchester Magistrates heard The court heard that Mr Funna, of Moorcroft Road, Northern Moor, who did not attend the hearing, was previously licensed by Trafford Council as a private hire driver He was subject to a complaint in January 2025 where it was alleged he had grabbed a passenger’s leg, pushed them and shouted at them When Council licensing enforcement officers investigated, they found Mr Funna had been suspended in September 2023 for failing to provide a medical report showing his fitness to drive, given his age, but that he had not returned his driver’s badges to Trafford Town Hall

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bury Bury killer who stabbed man to death with 'Call of Duty' knife has sentence appeal bid rejected Abbas Hussain was sentenced to seven years' detention Add to preferred sources Comments News Paul Britton Reporter 05:49, 17 Nov 2026 Updated 07:17, 1 Judges have rejected a bid to review a killer's custodial sentence. Abbas Hussain was sentenced to seven years' detention in a Young Offender Institution in April this year for manslaughter He stabbed Mohammed Isa Afzal, 19, to death with a 'Call of Duty-type' knife in the car park of a five-a-side football complex in Bury in the summer of 2025. Hussain was 19 at the time, and 20 when he was sentenced The incident took place at the Power League complex on Market Street in Bury town centre Hussain, of Windsor Crescent, Prestwich , was convicted of manslaughter after a trial at Manchester Crown Court . He was also found guilty of possession of an offensive weapon. He was found not guilty of a charge of murder The case was referred to the Attorney General’s Office for consideration, with the sentence subsequently referred up to the Court of Appeal by the office under the Unduly Lenient Sentence scheme

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Rochdale 'A sad day for College Bank and for Rochdale' as Seven Sisters tower blocks to be demolished After a decade of limbo for residents living in the iconic tower blocks - a decision on the future of the Seven Sisters has been made Add to preferre Residents of the Seven Sisters tower blocks in Rochdale have been left saddened, angered and disappointed after learning their homes are going to be bulldozed Rochdale Boroughwide Housing (RBH) have made the decision to demolish the 766 flats and replace them with a mix of 601 new flats and townhouses. The decision brings to an end an era of uncertainty for the towers, actually called College Bank, which were first earmarked for demoli What used to be a bustling community on the outskirts of Rochdale town centre now sits silent. That’s because only around 80 households remain from the original 766 since the original demolition announcement 10 years ago The uncertainty about the blocks' future has led many tenants to move on. Even hardened campaigners from the Save the Seven Sisters (ST7S) group have gone The campaigners have fought to stop demolition ever since it was first mentioned in 2016. They want to see the 1960s block refurbished instead

Kyle Howard, 36, called the police on May 25 this year to report that he had killed his wife, Keeley Aspinall, at their home on Tweedale Street, in Rochdale He told cops he had stabbed Ms Aspinall to death two days earlier, and was reporting his crime because her body was 'beginning to smell', Greater Manchester Police said Officers arrived at their home and found the 44-year-old deceased and concealed underneath a bed. The situation has now left the council with a toxic problem to deal with Town hall bosses are set to carry out ‘urgent’ works at Royton Library due to the need to tackle toxic asbestos. Asbestos is a fibrous mineral that was valued for its strength and fireproofing capabilities in old buildings and was widely used It is now banned from use, but if disturbed where it is still present, those fibres cause severe, incurable lung diseases. Around 5,000 people are estimated to die from asbestos-related issues every year The library was refurbished as part of a major £4m scheme which finished in 2024. However, earlier this year, the library had to shut suddenly and has remained closed since A council report said that in July 2026, library staff ‘reported that flooring in certain areas was becoming ‘bouncy’’ and ‘severe signs of dry rot’ were later discovered. Further investigations were carried out once the library closed

The 14-year-old, targeted just 100 yards from his home, died a short time later in hospital The still unsolved 1993 murder marked a new low in the bloody turf wars that had scarred Moss Side and earned the city a new, unwanted label – 'Gunchester' . evidence_packet.evidence_text: Stockport People left feeling threatened and intimidated as masked group march through Stockport The protest has been widely condemned. Stockport's council leader Coun Mark Roberts said: "We will not allow division to undermine the strong communities Stopfordians were left ‘feeling intimidated and threatened’ after balaclava-clad people marched through the town centre and ‘targeted’ public officials, an MP has said On November 15, people were seen marching through Stockport wearing balaclavas behind a banner appearing to protest houses of multiple occupation (HMOs) and asylum seekers . evidence_packet.evidence_text: The decision was made by just seven votes to six at a fractious planning committee meeting last night Share on WhatsApp Share via Email A visual showing the proposed Carrington Relief Road Trafford councillors have narrowly approved plans for the controversial Carrington Relief Road, despite hundreds of objections and warnings about the impact on Green Belt land and wildlife The decision was made by just seven votes to six at a fractious planning committee meeting last night, with members of the public gallery reportedly shouting "it's a disgrace" as the result was announced The road is considered essential to unlocking New Carrington, Trafford's largest housing and employment allocation, which could eventually deliver around 5,000 homes and 350,000 square metres of employment space Although the route lies around three miles north of Altrincham, the development could have wider implications for traffic, housing demand and public services across the borough The approximately 4km road would link the A6144 Manchester Road near Carrington and Partington with the Carrington Spur towards Sale

title: Man who defrauded Lincolnshire firm ordered to pay back 44k

evidence_packet.title: Man who defrauded Lincolnshire firm ordered to pay back 44k
evidence_packet.lead: Brian Sinclair, 54, used his position at Nobel Foods in North Scarle, Lincolnshire, to divert stock and place false orders with manufacturers to steal from the company, police said Sinclair, of Wild Street, Shaw, in Oldham, previously admitted one count of theft, four counts of f
evidence_packet.summary: Brian Sinclair, 54, used his position at Nobel Foods in North Scarle, Lincolnshire, to divert stock and place false orders with manufacturers to steal from the company, police said Sinclair, of Wild Street, Shaw, in Oldham, previously admitted one count of theft, four counts of f
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Brian Sinclair, 54, used his position at Nobel Foods in North Scarle, Lincolnshire, to divert stock and place false orders with manufacturers to steal from the company, police said Sinclair, of Wild Street, Shaw, in Oldham, previously admitted one count of theft, four counts of fraud by false representation and two counts of fraud by abuse of position He was sentenced to three years and eight months in prison at Lincoln Crown Court in April A proceeds of crime hearing at the same court earlier heard Sinclair made a benefit of £101,000 from his crimes, with available assets in the region of £44,000, including two pensions Recorder Anna Marie Trussler ordered the sum to be confiscated from Sinclair and to be paid to Nobel Foods in the form of compensation Sinclair, who watched the hearing via a video-link from prison, was given three months to pay back the money or face a further 12 months imprisonment

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester City Council can announce that Portland Street will be reopened to traffic from the early hours of Wednesday morning (November 4) This follows an extensive programme of emergency repairs due to a broken water main which ruptured last week A large-scale operation was put into action to isolate the source of the leak and repair it, and then carry out a full repair and resurface of the damaged road Crews from United Utilities and the Council have worked around the clock since Friday afternoon to ensure that the road could be reopened as quickly and safely as possible. This has been alongside TfGM staff who have also put additional resource into redirecting affected public t Illustrating the scale of the repairs needed, roughly 600 tonnes of road surface has been planed away and replaced over the course of these works The restrictions on the road are planned to be removed early on Wednesday morning (November 4), with the road practicably useable to motorists shortly after that

evidence_packet.evidence_text: New plans to boost air quality across Manchester between now and 2040 are being brought forward by the Council Manchester’s air quality has improved significantly in recent years due to investment in public transport and cycling and walking routes, cleaner vehicle technology including electric vehicles and stricter national emissions standards. The investment-led Greater Manchester Clean But while good progress has been made, the Council wants to go further because environmental air pollution remains a real health risk, especially for people in more disadvantaged communities or with existing health conditions who can be more vulnerable to its effects The Vision is simple: “Manchester will be a city where everyone can breathe cleaner air and live healthier lives.” Alongside it sits a headline action plan which will guide further measures to improve air quality across the city, based around four priorities Reduce people’s exposure to air pollution, prioritising the most vulnerable such as children and people with existing health conditions and communities where the potential health benefits are the greatest

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Residents in Saddleworth will have the opportunity to vote on the future of planning in their area when a referendum takes place on Thursday 10 December 2026 The referendum will ask residents whether they want Oldham Council and the Peak District National Park Authority to use the Saddleworth Neighbourhood Plan to help decide planning applications in the area The plan sets out local planning policies for Saddleworth and, if approved, will become part of the area’s statutory Development Plan, helping to guide decisions on future planning applications Residents will be asked the following question “Do you want Oldham Council and the Peak District National Park Authority to use the Neighbourhood Plan for Saddleworth to help it decide planning applications in the neighbourhood area?” To vote, residents must be registered to vote in local government elections and have a qualifying address within the Saddleworth Neighbourhood Area

title: Could you be Royton North's next councillor? By-election nominations close this Friday

evidence_packet.title: Could you be Royton North's next councillor? By-election nominations close this Friday
evidence_packet.lead: People are invited to step forward and make a difference in their community
evidence_packet.summary: People are invited to step forward and make a difference in their community
evidence_packet.evidence_text: People are invited to step forward and make a difference in their community Anyone interested in representing local residents and helping to make decisions affecting the area are invited to consider putting themselves forward as a candidate for the Royton North By-Election. Nominations close at 4pm this Friday (6 November 2026) The by-election has been called following a vacancy in the ward. If there is only one candidate nominated, then that candidate would be elected without contest. If more than one valid nomination is received, residents will go to the polls on Thursday 3 December 2026 to elect thei This is an opportunity for local people from all backgrounds to represent the interests of their community, raise issues that matter to residents and play a direct role in shaping the future of Royton North and the wider borough. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Cheers to the women who changed the way we drink! Hear the hidden history of the female pioneers who drank, distilled, and defied , while enjoying cocktails inspired by them Drinking history expert Simon Sharp takes you on a journey from the invention of the pub and modern beer, to distillation and champagne – where women have been at the forefront , challenging patriarchy so we can all enjoy a drink To illustrate these stories guests will enjoy four cocktails; The Mansplainer, The Poinsettia, Bees Knees, and Hanky Panky – all invented or inspired by these trailblazing ladies, crafted with ingredients sourced from female founded and led businesses A tribute to women’s creativity and courage , this tasting celebrates the mark they’ve left on drinking culture Simon Sharp is a history geek, drinks expert, and spirits judge. He travels around the country hosting tastings and talks revolving around the history of drinking. He has also appeared on radio, podcasts, and newspapers expressing his enthusiasm for drinking history and culture Are you more independent or community focused? Experimental or measured? Prefer work or play? Take our quick quiz to find out which radical you are!

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wednesday 12 May 2027 – Band on the Wall Thursday 13 May 2027 – Southbank Centre Sona Jobarteh is the first professional female kora virtuoso to emerge from any of West Africa’s five Griot dynasties, and a singer, composer and bandleader whose concerts fill some of the world’s finest halls. In 2026 she sold out the Elbphilharmonie in Hamburg, played Munich’s Prinzregententheater and the Schleswig-Holstein Musik Festival, and on October 11 received the Silicon Valley African Film Festival’s 2026 Icon Award for her contributions to African music, scholarship and cultural promotion. On stage, Sona sings and plays the 21-string kora and guitar, joined by Eric Appapoulay, also on guitar, Andi McLean on bass, Yuval Wetzler on drums, Anselmo Neto on percussion and her son, Sidiki Jobarteh, on balafon. The show blends Mandé griot tradition with blues, Afropop and contemporary songwriting. She has also toured with blues legend Taj Mahal. Her concerts have become events wherever she plays. She has performed more than a hundred shows across Europe, Africa, the United States and beyond, in some of the world’s most prestigious theaters and festivals, with sell-outs at London’s Barbican, Cologne’s Philharmonie and the Seine Musicale in Paris, and appearances at the Hollywood Bowl, Symphony Space in New York and WOMAD Australia and New Zealand. Her latest album, Badinyaa Kumoo, was named one of the best albums of its year by Songlines Magazine, and her single “Gambia” has passed 32 million YouTube views. Recent collaborations include a feature on LL Cool J’s album The FORCE, on the song “Black Code Suite”, and a guest appearance on “Se a Vida Pede” from the Brazilian group Gilsons’ latest album. evidence_packet.summary: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live […] The post Beat the Jams Autumn season announced appeared first on Band on the Wall
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live series showcases the very best of the jazz scene, at short rush hour gigs from 6pm at Band on the Wall. What better way to avoid those endless queues, chaotic traffic and stressful homeward journeys? Clock off and skip the rush-hour traffic while you watch live jazz and make the most of our happy hour deals from 5–7pm: £4.50 pints / 2 for £15 cocktails / £15 bottles of wine + pizzas from £5! The new season kicks off on 24 September with tenor saxophonist Dean Masser and pianist Richard Wetherall, followed by: 7 October – Anna Chandler-King Quartet Leeds based saxophonist and composer Anna joins us again for Beat the Jams, this time with her own band. Anna’s thoughtful and inventive compositions are firm favourites of us at Beat the Jams and her quartet promises to be a unique rush hour busting treat! 16 November – Sam Lightwing Quartet Saxophonist and composer Sam Lightwing brings presents brand new music for his thrilling young quartet, showcasing Sam’s original compositions, which blend classic mainstream jazz grooves with modern flavours of post-pop and latin, all wrapped up in the language of contemporary sax giants such as Chris Potter, Seamus Blake and Joshua Redman. 15 December – Svarc/Devine/Walsh with Richard Iles The band combines deep pocket, fearless interplay and a shared love of exploration. Expect everything from soulful melodies and infectious rhythms to moments of exhilarating collective improvisation, delivered with the chemistry that only world-class musicians can create. Tickets from £13 per show, or £42 for a season ticket

Whether your child already attends our Saturday Music Club, or just wants to try something new, our Young Musician’s Summer School is suitable for all abilities! evidence_packet.evidence_text: Joshua Reed-Cooper and Mike Thomas will bring regional French cooking and an extensive wine list to the former TNQ site this winter Go to Manchester's Finest X profile The duo behind Stockport’s Michelin-recognised Cantaloupe are opening a new French restaurant in the Northern Quarter Joshua Reed-Cooper and Mike Thomas will open Rasade at 108 High Street – the former site of long-standing bistro TNQ – this winter, with a menu inspired by regional French cooking and built around seasonal produce The new restaurant is the latest project from the pair, who have worked in some of the city’s most notable kitchens Cooper’s CV includes Where The Light Gets In , Adam Reid at The French and mana , while he also ran Tine, a pop-up kitchen at Blossom Street Social. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Counter Manchester , the much-anticipated new restaurant from Open Restaurant Group , opens its doors today at 12pm. It is the group’s first opening in Manchester city centre and brings a theatrical approach to dining to the heart of the city Led by acclaimed chef Andrew Sheridan, Counter is located in Manchester’s Island Building on John Dalton Street and has 60 covers. It is Open Restaurant Group’s ninth restaurant to date and its second site in Greater Manchester, following the launch of Arcadian in Didsbury in Sep At the focus of the restaurant is a four-to-five-seat chef’s counter, which places guests directly at the pass for an up-close view of the kitchen in action. The interiors feature four-metre elm trees, curved booth seating and a brass wine display, so the atmosphere and experienc Award-winning Andrew Sheridan brings his internationally inspired approach to Counter, building on a career that has seen multiple restaurants under his direction feature in the prestigious Michelin Guide. At Counter, he challenges convention by exploring what British cooking can The menu puts this philosophy into practice with dishes that combine unexpected ingredients and inventive flavour pairings. Highlights include the Beef Tartare Pressed Croissant, pairing aged beef with a crispy pressed croissant, smoked oyster mayo, wasabi and pickled shallot and From the grill, guests can enjoy the Satay Spatchcock Chicken, served with peanut satay, fermented chilli, coconut, burnt lime and crispy shallot, alongside the slow-cooked Thai Lamb Shoulder, served with red thai sauce, chilli and coriander

evidence_packet.lead: The government's new Digital and Technologies Jobs Plan aims to create 200,000 entry-level jobs over the next decade, recognising the barriers facing employers and the importance of regional organisations in connecting people with opportunities.
evidence_packet.summary: The government's new Digital and Technologies Jobs Plan aims to create 200,000 entry-level jobs over the next decade, recognising the barriers facing employers and the importance of regional organisations in connecting people with opportunities. The government has published its D
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The government's new Digital and Technologies Jobs Plan aims to create 200,000 entry-level jobs over the next decade, recognising the barriers facing employers and the importance of regional organisations in connecting people with opportunities. The government has published its D The plan acknowledges that the challenge is not simply a shortage of people with digital skills. Entry-level recruitment has become more difficult, with employers increasingly favouring experienced candidates and many graduates and other new entrants struggling to secure their fi Manchester Digital contributed to the development of the plan through its involvement in the government's Digital Skills Council, drawing on its work with employers and education providers across Greater Manchester Around 800,000 digital and technology roles are projected to need filling over the next decade. The plan sets out an ambition to create 200,000 entry-level jobs, including apprenticeships, during that period The plan also addresses how AI is changing workforce requirements and the importance of ensuring people entering the industry have both technical knowledge and practical workplace skills Manchester Digital's 2026 Sector Insights Report highlighted a reduction of around 20% in early-career opportunities, despite continued demand for experienced technology professionals

The title is the Latin plural of “asylum”, which can mean both a place of refuge and an institution for the insane – and the piece plays on this plurality. Its third movement, Ecstasio , is s Between these two pieces comes a world premiere: Gabriella Smith’s How To Be A Bird , written for tonight’s soloist Pekka Kuusisto. Hailed by the LA Times as “an outright sensation”, Smith writes music drawn from field recordings and underwater microphones, looking for what she c The evening closes with Stravinsky’s Firebird Suite , one of the happiest accidents in musical history. Sergei Diaghilev, head of the Ballets Russes, saw his first three choices to score a new ballet fall through before he gambled on an unproven 27-year-old; Stravinsky himself la Four works, then, that each began as a risk on someone (to varying degrees) untested – Stravinsky in 1910, Adès in 1996, Smith tonight. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Football Mauricio Pochettino Mauricio Pochettino 'begins Man United job early' as staff fly into UK to work Mauricio Pochettino is not expected to take the reins of Manchester United until later this week, but his staff are making a head start at Old Trafford Add to preferr Mauricio Pochettino's backroom staff have already arrived at Manchester United , as they look to pick up the pieces of a torrid start to the Premier League season. That's despite the Argentine head coach not arriving at Old Trafford until later this week The 54-year-old is committed to navigating a CONCACAF quarter-final double header with the United States national team before starting the next chapter of his career at the Theatre of Dreams. The Stars and Bars enjoyed a 6-0 rout of their Caribbean neighbours on Saturday in Miami As a result, Pochettino will not touch down on UK soil until the dust settles on that encounter. However, with the deficit being so big, the head coach has allowed his backroom staff to fly into Greater Manchester early to prepare for his arrival Jesus Perez, Toni Jimenez and Sebastian Pochettino - who is the son of Mauricio - flew into the north west on Saturday. While Miguel D'Adostino has remained Stateside with Pochettino, he is also expected to join the head coach when he officially takes up tenure with United on Nov It comes as Pochettino has his work cut out for him should he harbour any ambitions of turning the tide with the Reds. At the time of writing, the club sits 18th in the Premier League standings on eight points, having won just one of their opening 10 matches

После выхода хита «Kasaba» в 2008 году Мурат Далкылыч стал одной из главных фигур турецкой поп-музыки. Он известен своим узнаваемым голосом, энергичными выступлениями и популярными песнями, среди которых «Bir Güzellik Yap». За годы карьеры в музыке, написании песен и кино он приобрел большую и преданную аудиторию как в Турции, так и за ее пределами. 29 января 2027 года Мурат Далкылыч выступит в indigo at The O2 в Лондоне. Вас ждет яркий вечер турецкой поп-музыки, живого исполнения и любимых хитов. Не упустите возможность увидеть Мурата Далкылыча вживую в Лондоне! Предварительный заказ
